That being said, it is also important to put virtual currency in perspective as a payment

Administrators of other major centralized virtual currencies report processing similar transaction

This relative volume of transactions becomes important when you consider that,
according to the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, the best estimate for the amount of
all global criminal proceeds available for laundering through the financial system in 2009 was
$1.6 trillion.

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) — Suspicious activity reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: No. 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements are not triggered on these facts because the fact pattern does not identify a financial institution subject to SAR duties or any suspicious transaction requiring a report.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates the Secretary to require a “financial institution” to report “any suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation,” and provides related protections (e.g., safe harbor and confidentiality). Element-by-element: (1) Covered reporter: § 5318(g) applies to a “financial institution” with SAR obligations imposed by regulation; the facts describe only an individual (SYN_7a40347d) and do not identify any bank/MSB/other covered financial institution involved or obligated to file a SAR, so this element cannot be confirmed. (2) Suspicious transaction: the listed activity consists of four small inbound ACH/wire transfers ($250.65–$846.34) labeled as “small inbound donation,” with total volume not obviously inconsistent with the declared expected monthly volume (~$4,949); the facts provide no indicators of illegality (e.g., fraud, structuring, sanctions evasion) or other basis to deem the transactions “suspicious” under § 5318(g). Because both the existence of a covered financial institution reporter and the presence of a suspicious transaction are not established, applicability cannot be determined from the provided facts, even though “§ 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting” is the relevant statutory framework.
